title: ISO/IEC 7816-3 smartcard interface (conditional-access card reader): T=0 / T=1 characters, RX ring and TX buffer over AXI4
features: Card pins: sc_vcc_en, sc_rst_n, sc_clk (clk / (2 * (CLK_DIV + 1))), open-drain I/O (sc_io_in, sc_io_oe_low), sc_det (card present).

Activation (CMD.activate): VCC on, CLK running, RST low for RST_CLKS card clocks, then RST high (STATUS.active); deactivation (CMD.deactivate, card removal or ENABLE off): RST low, CLK stopped, VCC off.
Characters: start bit, 8 data bits, even parity; one ETU is ETU card clocks (F / D); direct or inverse convention (CTRL.inverse).

T=0: parity errors are signalled to the card (I/O low 10.5..12 ETU) and the character is not stored; a character the card rejects is sent again 2 ETU later, up to 4 times, then the TX fails (STATUS.tx_fail, PERR). T=1: no signalling, the parity flag is stored.
RX: every character goes as one word {23'b0, parity_err, data} through an 8-word FIFO to the ring at RING_BASE (RING_WORDS words, WR_IDX / RD_IDX); a full FIFO drops characters (OVF_CNT).
TX: CMD.tx_start sends TX_LEN bytes read from TX_ADDR (byte i in word i / 4, little-endian), start to start every 12 + GUARD ETU.
Waiting time: WT ETUs without a start bit after RST, the last character or a TX raise TIMEOUT.

fields.desc: interface on; 0 deactivates the card and clears WR_IDX
card clocks per ETU (F / D; 0 counts as 1)
extra guard time N in ETU
card clocks of RST low at activation
words (at least 2); move or resize the ring only while WR_IDX is below the new size, or with ENABLE 0 (which clears WR_IDX)
power the card and reset it (card present, ENABLE)
send TX_LEN bytes; ignored while a TX runs
the card is powered and out of reset
the last TX failed (repetitions exhausted or deactivation)
an AXI error response since the activation
next ring word the core writes
characters received with a parity error

irqs.name: RX
irqs.desc: a character is in the ring

irqs.name: PERR
irqs.desc: an RX parity error, or a TX that failed after 4 repetitions

irqs.name: TIMEOUT
irqs.desc: the waiting time passed without a character

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: an RX ring write or a TX buffer read saw an AXI error response

sequence: Write CTRL (enable, clk_div), TIMING (ETU 372 at first), WAITS, RING_BASE, RING_WORDS, RD_IDX = 0 and IRQ_ENABLE.
On DET with STATUS.present = 1 write CMD.activate = 1; read the ATR from the ring on RX (set CTRL.inverse if TS is 0x3F).
Put a command in the TX buffer, write TX_ADDR, TX_LEN and CMD.tx_start = 1; on TX_DONE check STATUS.tx_fail, then read the card's answer from the ring.
Write CMD.deactivate = 1 to power the card down.
notes: m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time.
RX ring writes use the write channel and TX buffer reads the read channel (two engines, one ID).
sc_vcc_en, sc_rst_n, sc_clk, sc_io_oe_low (out) and sc_io_in, sc_det (in) are the card pins; the I/O pad is open drain with a pull-up.
The core testbench prints one `LAT <master> dram R|W <cycles>` line per AXI burst (tb/tv_lat_mon.svh), the regression suite's latency format.
